title: Engineering Foundation and Technology Lock
outcome: A clean clone validates its design and machine contracts, bootstraps a thin Hermes Shim plus separately managed Python runtime, and runs deterministic Windows/Linux checks without implementing production Pipeline behavior.
prerequisites: Initial documentation baseline commit exists on main
Repository, product, package, license, and governance identities are accepted
module_boundaries: Thin Hermes Shim and authenticated Control Interface
Versioned contract authoring and generation toolchain
Controller transaction and persistence feasibility seams
Stage Executor and LangGraph authority boundary
Repository structure, architecture checks, deterministic fakes, and CI

slices.title: Repository baseline
slices.demonstration: A clean Windows or Linux clone identifies every normative entry point and rejects a deliberately broken Schema fixture.

slices.title: Python quality skeleton
slices.demonstration: The frozen canonical commands pass from a clean clone without credentials or public network after dependency installation.

slices.title: Contract toolchain
slices.demonstration: Valid fixtures round-trip and generated Schema/OpenAPI output has zero drift while invalid and secret-canary fixtures fail deterministically.

slices.title: Domain and persistence spikes
slices.demonstration: Fault injection restarts at every durable boundary without duplicate transition or stale advancement.

slices.title: Hermes Shim and runtime spike
slices.demonstration: A real Hermes Gateway delivers one authenticated fake command exactly once and either process can restart without forging or losing an acknowledged result.

slices.title: Agent and runtime security spikes
slices.demonstration: A hostile fixture cannot mutate Git, escape authorized roots, inherit a canary secret, or leave a child process alive after fencing.

slices.title: Foundation integration
slices.demonstration: A clean install runs a fake command from Hermes through the Shim/runtime and back, survives restart, exposes health evidence, and passes all mandatory checks on the exact Candidate.

invariants: The Hermes-loaded Shim remains dependency-light and has no Pipeline authority
The managed runtime owns Controller state and exposes only authenticated loopback Interfaces
Controller domain code has no LangGraph or Adapter dependency
LangGraph is confined to Stage execution
Agents have no Git mutation or remote credentials
All external behavior is behind a typed Interface with a deterministic fake
Required CI uses no live model, provider credential, or public network
Every Slice is independently reviewable and leaves mandatory checks green

testing: Deterministic Windows/Linux required checks use no live model, provider credential, or public network
migration: Bootstrap Schema adoption, SQLite migration seam, and rollback feasibility are recorded; no production-state migration occurs
security: Negative tests prove path, process, environment, secret, descriptor, Agent, browser, and Git authority boundaries
documentation: README, policies, contract fixtures, commands, compatibility targets, feasibility decisions, and Closeout remain synchronized
demonstration: A real Hermes load reaches the isolated fake runtime and a complete fake command path survives restart on the exact integrated Candidate

exit_criteria.observable_result: The frozen uv environment synchronizes on supported Windows and Linux runners.
Formatting, lint, type, unit, contract, architecture, and offline integration checks pass.
Every committed Schema has valid and invalid fixtures plus a reproducible Pydantic, Schema, and OpenAPI drift check.
The Controller transaction spike proves atomic Inbox, Event, projection, and Outbox behavior, deduplication, revision conflict, crash recovery, and stale fencing.
SQLite workload evidence supports the declared version 1 concurrency envelope or triggers a replacement ADR.
LangGraph checkpoint and replay evidence proves it cannot independently advance Pipeline state.
A real Hermes installation loads the Shim and reaches a fake managed runtime through protected loopback transport.
Codex and OpenCode Adapters prove structured output, timeout, cancellation, bounded logs, and error classification.
An OpenCode E2E probe uses Chrome DevTools MCP in a clean Verification Sandbox without Git authority.
Security tests cover descriptor permissions, path escape, environment leakage, shell avoidance, secret canaries, and process-tree cleanup.
The hermes pipeline setup, doctor, start, status, and stop commands operate idempotently for the non-production skeleton.
Accepted decisions, feasibility results, limitations, exact commands, residual risks, and Phase 1 prerequisites are recorded in CLOSEOUT.md.

exclusions: Live Feishu or GitHub production operations
Real Project RBAC and approval workflows
Production Agent prompts or model-quality acceptance
Remote publication, PR creation, merge, deployment, or dashboard
Destructive migration or automatic update application

risks.description: Hermes cannot safely load or supervise the Thin Shim and managed-runtime topology.
risks.mitigation: Prove real source installation and lifecycle before product code.
risks.trigger: The Shim requires unmanaged third-party imports or cannot recover after restart.

risks.description: Windows or Linux cannot enforce a required Agent capability boundary.
risks.mitigation: Run hostile fixtures on both systems and fail closed for unsupported profiles.
risks.trigger: A fixture escapes authorized roots, inherits a canary, or leaves an unfenced process.

risks.description: SQLite cannot meet the declared single-Workspace workload or recovery envelope.
risks.mitigation: Measure queue depth, latency, WAL, backup, disk-full, and crash behavior.
risks.trigger: Limits exceed the declared envelope or an acknowledged command is lost or duplicated.

risks.description: LangGraph replay duplicates a Controller transition.
risks.mitigation: Persist command identity and receipt and fault-inject every checkpoint boundary.
risks.trigger: Replay appends a second business Event.

risks.description: Codex or OpenCode structured or cancellation interfaces are unstable.
risks.mitigation: Pin versions, capability-probe, classify errors, and preserve fallback evidence.
risks.trigger: Required structured result or process-tree cleanup cannot be guaranteed.

risks.description: Bootstrap contract candidates drift from the future Pydantic authoring source.
risks.mitigation: Complete adoption and zero-drift checks in slice-00-03 before behavior-bearing spikes.
risks.trigger: Generated output differs without an explicit contract version change.

risks.description: External provider polling or Feishu interception assumptions differ from real Hermes or GitHub behavior.
risks.mitigation: Use pinned upstream evidence and isolated real integration probes.
risks.trigger: Callback interception or conditional polling cannot be made idempotent.

stop_conditions: The Hermes plugin surface cannot safely host the Thin Shim
A supported platform cannot enforce required process or path boundaries
SQLite fails the declared workload or recovery proof
Codex or OpenCode lacks a stable structured and cancellation Interface
Chrome MCP cannot be isolated from development authority
A new dependency family, public service, or privileged helper becomes necessary
Repository identity or licensing blocks public distribution
